research_rationale:
Executive Order 11438 of December 3, 1968 (33 FR 18085), Prescribing Procedures Governing Interdepartmental Cash Awards to the Members of the Armed Forces, issued under 10 U.S.C. 1124(b) and (e) and 3 U.S.C. 301, has four numbered sections. Section 1 allows honorary recognition or a cash award for a suggestion, invention or scientific achievement of a member of the armed forces adopted by another executive department or agency, by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation. Section 2 lets the adopting agency recommend an award and requires awards under regulations of the two Secretaries. Section 3 caps a cash award at $25,000. Section 4 requires funds to be transferred from the recommending agency and procedures to be prescribed by the Civil Service Commission when several agencies benefit. The dossier's two-clause inventory ran sections 1 through 3 together, so I corrected it to four clauses with exact spans in the held Federal Register text. Later events, all amendments that leave the clauses continuing: (1) Executive Order 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055), section 2-101, lists EO 11438 among the orders in which Office of Personnel Management is substituted for Civil Service Commission, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; in EO 11438 that reference appears only in section 4. (2) Executive Order 13286 of February 28, 2003 (68 FR 10619), section 63, strikes the Secretary of Transportation in sections 1 and 2 and the Department of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 2 and 4, inserting Homeland Security, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92. The packet's chain also lists EO 12977 of October 19, 1995 as an amending actor; its held text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12977.txt) does not contain the number 11438 and the source-ladder queue file attributed to it holds pages of EO 13286, so it is not a later event. The U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; changes between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected) prints the order, as amended by EO 12107 and EO 13286 section 63, as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1124 with no ending statement. The held text of 10 U.S.C. 1124 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t10-s1124.txt) still authorizes these cash awards and limits them to $25,000, and the held current 5 CFR 451.101(b) (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t5-451.101.txt) states that section 4 of E.O. 11438 requires the Office of Personnel Management to prescribe procedures for covering the cost of a cash award recommended by more than one agency. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) show no revocation or supersession. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
